question: Write a function applyAll that takes an array and a callback, and calls the callback on every item. Log it with an array of numbers and n => n * 2.
Write a higher-order function called run that takes a callback and calls it with 'hello', then log run(msg => console.log('got ' + msg)).
Write a function mapAll that takes an array and a callback and returns a new array of results. Log mapAll over ['a','b'] with s => s.toUpperCase().
Write a function retry that takes a callback and a number of attempts, calls it, and logs 'attempt n' on each failure. Use it on a callback that fails twice then returns 'ok'.

Write a function attempt that takes a promise-returning callback, an attempt number and a total, and returns a promise resolving on success or retrying after a rejection. Log it for a fake that rejects twice then resolves.
Write a debounce function that takes a callback and a delay, and only calls it after the delay has passed with no new calls. Log it with a fake clock.
Write a debounce function and drive it with a fake clock so you can log exactly when the callback fires after three rapid calls. Show the fake clock advancing.
Write a throttle function that runs a callback immediately, then ignores calls for a window. Drive it with a fake clock and log which calls win.
Write a withLogging wrapper using a rest parameter that logs the arguments before calling the original and the result after. Log it with a two-argument function.
Write a function once that takes a callback and returns a function that runs it only the first time, logging on every call. Call the wrapped callback three times.
Write a spy function that wraps a callback, logs each call with its argument, keeps a count, and returns the original result. Log it twice then print the report.
Write a memoize function that caches callback results in a Map, logging 'hit' or 'miss'. Call the memoized double with 5, 5 and 6.
Write a groupBy that takes an array and a selector callback, returning an object of arrays keyed by the selector result. Log it over [1,2,3,4] with a parity selector.
Write a function sortBy that returns a comparator built from a selector callback, then log people sorted by age. People: [{n:'B',age:30},{n:'A',age:20}].
Write a function makeTimer that takes a callback and ms and returns a function starting the callback after that delay with setTimeout. Log 'done' after 5 milliseconds.
Write a function take that returns a function that calls the callback with the next value in a list, and logs 'done' when the list runs out. Log four pulls.
Write a function chain that takes two callbacks and returns a function running the first then feeding its result into the second. Log chain(addOne, double)(5).
Predict the output. Define an array of three arrow functions that each log their index, then call them in a for loop and log the order of the messages.
Write a function eachSeries that takes an array of callbacks and calls them one by one, collecting the results. Log it with three small callbacks.
Write a function curry that turns a three-argument callback into nested single-argument functions. Log curried(1)(2)(3) for a sum of three numbers.
Write a function compose that takes callbacks and returns one applying them right to left. Log compose(double, addOne)(5) and compose(addOne, double)(5).
Write a function pipe that takes callbacks and returns one applying them left to right, then log the same two callbacks to contrast with compose.
Write a function composeAll that applies three callbacks right to left and logs the running value at each step. Log it for double, addOne, squared on 3.
Predict the output. Build an array of callbacks from a map over numbers where each one logs its number, then call only the middle one and log how many callbacks exist.
Write a function reduceRightFn that takes a list of callbacks and a starting value, applying them from the right, then log the result for three doublers and addOne.
Write a function race that takes an array of promise-returning callbacks and returns a promise resolving with the first one to settle, logging the winner's label.
Write a function allSettledLite that takes an array of promise-returning callbacks and returns a promise with each result or error message. Log it for one resolve and one reject.
Write a function debounceCount that debounces a callback and also logs how many calls were dropped. Drive it with a fake clock and log the dropped count.
Write a function createQueue that takes a worker callback and returns enqueue and size, running the callback for each item. Log enqueuing two items.
Write a function createEmitter with on and emit methods closing over a map of event names to callbacks. Log one listener firing on emit.
Write a function flattenDeep that takes a nested array and a depth, and flattens up to that depth using flat. Log it for [1,[2,[3,[4]]]] with depth 2.
Predict the output. Show that map passes three arguments to its callback, by logging an arrow that takes only the first and one that names all three.
Write a function repeatEach that takes a number and a callback, and runs the callback that many times passing the step number. Log repeatEach(3) with a logging callback.
Write a function that returns an object with a run method closing over an array of callbacks, then logs the results of running all of them. Log three callbacks.
Write a function guard that takes a value and a fallback callback, returning the value unless it is null or undefined. Log it with null and with 0.
Write a function mapKeys that takes an object and a callback returning new key names, and returns a new object. Log it over {first: 1, last: 2} with k => k.toUpperCase().
Write a function throttleLeading that runs a callback on the first call and then at most once per window, driven by a fake clock. Log four calls spaced by the clock.
Write a function applyAsync that takes an array of promise-returning callbacks and a mapper callback, then logs each mapped result in order. Log two tasks.
Predict the output. Log a callback passed straight into forEach without wrapping, and log what Array.from does with a callback on the string 'abc'.
Write a function createScheduler that takes a callback and returns a run method which collects calls made in the same tick and logs them together. Log a run and three pushes.
Write a function applyWithIndex that takes an array and a callback, and logs 'item:index' for each. Log it for ['x', 'y'].
